question: Is the v2.1 format direction d (layer 16, native minus pasted) just a generic verbosity knob? We compare it with a 'detailed vs brief' instruction direction l in the style of Stolfo et al. (ICLR 2025), remove l's component from d, and check whether d still lengthens pasted answers and still brings them closer to native than a same-norm pure length push does.
builds_on: transfer v1 (registered 2026-11-27). Its open-group length effect was seen in an interim look at 68/81 units before this registration. The quantities registered here (effects of d_perp, d_par and a pure length vector) have not been observed.
pinned_sha256_from: transfer/protocol.json (same files, checked again at preflight)

inputs.units: transfer v1 units.jsonl (SHA256 in the registration)
inputs.direction_units: the other 294 units (short, structured, near, external); used only to estimate l
inputs.format_dirs: format_dirs.pt from length_control/build.py: d_L = mean v2.1 ordinary (nat - flat) at layers 4..28; d_16 equals the vector used by transfer v1

instructions.detailed: Please give a detailed, thorough answer.

length_direction.insertion: the instruction's tokens are inserted right before the final <|im_end|> of the last user turn, in both the B and C prompt of each direction unit
length_direction.estimate: l_L = mean over direction units and both forms of h_L(detailed) - h_L(brief) at the last prompt token, layers 4..28 (block outputs, same convention as v2.1)
length_direction.phase: computed in the same run before any generation; saved with cos(d_L, l_L) per layer

vectors_at_layer_16.d_par: (d . l_hat) l_hat, the part of d along the length direction
vectors_at_layer_16.len: l_hat scaled to |d| (a pure length push with d's norm)

site: block 16 output; last prompt token at prefill and every generated token; alpha 1 (as transfer v1)
length: n = generated tokens excluding the stop token (all tokens at the cap), floored at 1

analysis.uncertainty: history-cluster bootstrap, 4000 resamples, numpy seed 453, two-sided 95% percentile intervals (one joint decision)
analysis.M_manipulation_check: mean log n(C_plus_len) - log n(C); the length vector must lengthen answers (lower bound > 0), else the control is invalid
analysis.S_len: mean idx(KL_B(C_plus_len), KL_B(C_plus_d)) with idx(x, y) = (x - y)/(x + y), 0 if both 0; positive means d brings C closer to B than a same-norm pure length push

decision.not_just_length: M valid, L_perp lower bound > 0 and S_len lower bound > 0
decision.mostly_length: M valid, L_perp interval inside [-0.05, 0.05] and S_len upper bound <= 0.05

secondary: length shifts of C_plus_d, C_plus_dpar, C_plus_len and C_plus_dperp relative to C
agreement of B, C and C_plus_d token streams with the transfer v1 run on the same GPU
not_claimed: A single instruction contrast defines l; other verbosity directions may exist. Removing one direction does not remove all length information. No claim about other layers, models, or answer quality.
